title: The Artist's Toolkit
objective: After this level you can name the basic elements of art: line, shape, color, texture and space.
summary: Every artwork is built from the elements of art: line, shape, color, texture and space (many lists add form). Even empty space has a shape.

cards.headline: Every picture ever made uses the same few building blocks.
cards.body: A cave wall, a comic, the icon on your phone: artists build them all from what they call the elements of art. Learn five of them and you can take any picture apart.

cards.headline: Line and shape
cards.body: Start with line: a mark longer than it is wide. It can be straight or curved, thick or thin. Close a line into a loop and you have a shape. Shapes are flat and come in two families: geometric, like squares and circles, or organic, the free-form shapes you find in nature. A smiley face is one circle, two dots and a curve. Line and shape, doing all the work.

cards.headline: Color and texture
cards.body: Color is light reflected off things (Level 4 is all about it). Texture is how a surface feels, or looks like it would feel. It can be real, like thick paint you could touch, or only implied. A drawing of a porcupine can look prickly, but run your finger over it and the paper is smooth. The prickles are an illusion.

cards.fact: Empty space has a shape too.
cards.context: Space is the area around and between things. The empty part is called negative space, and it has a shape of its own: think of the hole in the letter O. Space also means the feeling of depth, when a flat picture seems to open up like a window. That's the five: line, shape, color, texture and space. Many lists add form, meaning 3D shapes like balls and boxes.

cards.headline: Toolkit: unpacked
learned: Line: a mark longer than it is wide
Shape: a closed line, geometric or organic
Color is reflected light; texture can be real or implied
Space includes negative space and the feeling of depth

questions.prompt: In the elements of art, what is a shape?

options.label: A mark longer than it is wide

questions.explanation: Close a line into a loop and you get a flat shape, geometric or organic.

questions.prompt: A painted velvet cushion looks soft, but the canvas feels hard. What is the painter using?

options.label: Negative space
options.rationale: Negative space is the empty area around things.

options.label: Geometric shape
options.rationale: Squares and circles don't make anything look soft.

options.label: Form
options.rationale: Form is a real 3D shape, like a ball or a box.

questions.explanation: Implied texture only looks like it would feel a certain way, like the porcupine drawing that's smooth to the touch.

questions.prompt: Level 1's hand stencil: pigment was blown around a hand, so the hand itself is bare rock. Which element makes the hand appear?

options.label: Implied texture
options.rationale: The rock's feel isn't what shows the hand.

options.label: Geometric shape
options.rationale: A hand is an organic shape, and nobody painted it.

options.label: A thick line
options.rationale: No one drew the outline; it's where the pigment stopped.

questions.explanation: The hand is the empty, unpainted area: negative space, which has a shape of its own.
